method: Layout-blind periodic table text, fitted on public Currier B pages only. Words are drawn independently by frequency from the public Currier B word list; every tenth word (ten being the commonest paragraph line length on the public B pages) is drawn from the words ending in m, all others from the words not ending in m. The writer never sees where a line ends. This is the strongest procedure of its kind I could find: periods 8 to 13 were tried on the practice split and none lifts the line-final to mid-line ratio above about 1.0, against 61.6 for the manuscript there. Sent as a best attempt that does not land: F-001 survives every generator that cannot see the line break. It says nothing about language, though; a writer who can see the line end and puts an m-final word there would reproduce it, and the attack format (a word stream re-cut to the hidden line shapes) cannot express such a rule.
